411	                         - self.__starttag_text.rfind("\n")  # noqa: E127

I fixed the bug: the `` example now renders as a single paragraph, with the comment kept inside it. All 388 block and inline syntax tests pass, including three new ones. I couldn't run the full suite cleanly here (explained below). **Cause:** In `markdown/htmlparser.py`, when an HTML comment (or another block-level item) sits at the start of a line and isn't inside a raw HTML block, it's pulled out as a standalone block. That's correct when a comment interrupts ordinary paragraph text. But `` isn't a block-level tag, so it's treated as inline HTML inside a paragraph. The parser didn't notice the comment was inside an open `` and split it out, which inserted the `

` … `

`. **Fix (in `markdown/htmlparser.py`):** - The parser now keeps a list of inline tags that are open in the current paragraph. A tag is added when it opens and removed when it closes. - While any inline tag is open, a comment at the start of a line stays in the paragraph instead of becoming a separate block. - A blank line, or the start of a raw HTML block, clears the list. That way an inline tag that's never closed, like a stray ``, doesn't affect anything after its paragraph ends. Everything else behaves as before. For example, `Some text\n\nmore` still splits into two paragraphs with the comment between them. **Tests:** I added three cases to `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py`: the reported `` example, a comment after an inline tag that has already closed (still split out), and a comment after an unclosed inline tag followed by a blank line (still split out). **Full suite:** Running everything gives a large number of failures that come from this environment, not the change: - `tests/test_apis.py` and `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py` fail to import because the `yaml` module isn't installed. - About 166 extension tests fail with errors like `No module named 'toc'` or `'footnotes'`. That suggests the package isn't installed in the venv, so extensions can't be loaded by their short names. I didn't install anything to fix this, as instructed. I also couldn't get permission to run those suites against the original code for a direct comparison.
